faq.a: Chronic inflammation and viral replication increase basal metabolic rate and promote muscle breakdown.
faq.q: Why does HIV cause wasting even with adequate food intake?

faq.a: ART improves viral control and often leads to weight gain, but concurrent nutrition and infection treatment are essential.
Empiric treatment for common parasites (e.g., albendazole) while arranging referral for diagnostics.
faq.q: What is the first step if a stool test is unavailable?

exam: What bedside measurements would you use to diagnose HIV wasting in a clinic without a scale? — Use MUAC (<22 cm) and serial weight checks if possible; document >10 % loss over 6 months.

A patient on ART presents with 12 % weight loss, chronic diarrhoea, and CD4 150. What is your next investigation and why? — Order stool microscopy for parasites and a chest X‑ray (or TB symptom screen) to identify treatable infections driving wasting.
How does TB co‑infection exacerbate HIV-associated wasting? — TB adds systemic inflammation, increases energy expenditure, and causes anorexia, accelerating weight loss.
Why is serum albumin not a reliable sole marker of nutritional status in HIV wasting? — It falls with inflammation independent of intake; weight trend is more informative.
When would you consider prescribing megestrol acetate for a wasting patient? — After optimising ART and treating infections, if weight loss continues >5 % over 4 weeks despite nutritional support.

Explain how you would counsel a patient with limited food resources to improve caloric intake. — Emphasise frequent small meals, use locally available protein (beans, eggs), add oil or groundnuts for calories, and hydrate with oral rehydration solution.
What are the red‑flag signs that require urgent referral for a patient with HIV wasting? — Rapid >15 % weight loss in 1 month, persistent fever, severe dehydration, or new neurological signs.

Distinguish HIV wasting from cancer cachexia in terms of pathophysiology and clinical clues. — Both involve cytokine‑mediated catabolism, but cancer cachexia often has a known tumour, may present with night pain, and lacks opportunistic infections.
ai.title: HIV-Associated Wasting Syndrome
ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: HIV-associated wasting is a multifactorial loss of lean body mass in advanced HIV, driven by chronic inflammation, opportunistic infections, and inadequate intake. Recognising it early guides targeted treatment and improves survival in low‑resource settings.

b: Prevalence up to 30% in untreated HIV in sub‑Saharan Africa
Associated with CD4 <200 cells/µL and high viral load
sections.p: Wasting syndrome is defined by >10% involuntary weight loss or BMI <18 kg/m² plus at least two of: chronic diarrhoea, fever, or night sweats in an HIV‑positive adult. It reflects severe disease (WHO stage 3/4) and predicts mortality.

b: Opportunistic infections (TB, CMV, cryptosporidiosis) worsen loss
Micronutrient deficiencies impair appetite and metabolism
sections.p: The syndrome results from a combination of increased resting energy expenditure, malabsorption, reduced intake, and catabolic cytokines (TNF‑α, IL‑1).

b: Weight loss >5 % in 1 month or >10 % in 6 months is a red flag
Low albumin (<30 g/L) often accompanies severe wasting
sections.p: Wasting worsens immune function, delays ART response, and increases risk of opportunistic infections and mortality. Early identification allows nutritional and pharmacologic interventions.

t.b: Screening tool when scales unavailable; <22 cm suggests severe wasting
Detects anemia, opportunistic infection risk; CD4 <200 cells/µL supports advanced disease
Identify chronic diarrhoea causes (e.g., Cryptosporidium); treatable infections improve weight
Assess protein status; low values indicate poor nutrition
Screen for TB, a common cause of wasting; if unavailable, use clinical TB scoring

b: Start/optimise ART promptly; avoid protease inhibitors with severe liver disease
Treat identified infections (e.g., TB with rifampicin‑based regimen, cryptosporidiosis with nitazoxanide if available)
Micronutrient supplementation: vitamin A, zinc, selenium
Consider appetite stimulants (megestrol acetate) only if weight loss persists despite nutrition
sections.p: Treat underlying infections, optimise ART, and provide nutritional support. Monitor weight weekly.

Cancer cachexia often has a known malignancy and may present with night sweats
sections.p: Distinguish HIV wasting from malnutrition due to food insecurity alone, and from cancer cachexia.

sections.p: Serum albumin falls in inflammation independent of nutrition; a normal albumin does not rule out wasting.
